guidance: The centrepiece holds the tape: a glass dome on a plinth at the plaza corner with the tape glowing above it, seen while working the plaza
The rooftop ski jump points straight down at the Pagoda; the remake adds red and green edge stripes (LP12 34:29)
The fountain sculpture's trench runs towards the neighbouring walkway, and Fountain Gap is on the checklist
Letters behind glass (K in a display window; T and E in rooms entered through windows) teach that windows are doors
Hidden on purpose: the walkway climb, the T room, the clocktower bowl, cop car 3 'tucked away in the shadows'
The guide frames the level as several dedicated runs: all five tapes in one run 'will be impossible' (G1 p115)
designLogic: Climb then drop: the tape is lower than its launch; height is earned on walkways and spent in one falling air through glass
Show the target, hide the door: the tape is on the most visible object, but the entrance is the fountain a block away
A named gap opens the route (Fountain Gap) and another closes it (Pagoda Gap)
Speed management is the skill: gain (corner quarter pipe), keep (trench), brake (walkways), regain, then the ski jump's drop
Stats gate on top of the skill gate: 'Only characters with their attributes built up will be able to get to the tape' (G1 p122)
Time gate: 'every second of time on the clock to get into position' (G1 p122); the level is built for dedicated runs
Secret rooms interlock: the T room and spiral top give the TAS a second high platform to the Pagoda
One letter per district tours the whole level; G1's efficient order is K, S, E, T, A
Failure is visible: a short ski jump lands the skater beneath the tape he just missed
The career's synthesis: quarter-pipe speed, walkway precision, hidden roof access (as in Downtown), a long committed launch (as in Downhill Jam) and flying through glass (as in Warehouse)
Scores are not the reward: Lombard Gap 5000 and the spiral grinds outscore Pagoda Gap 1000
The remake keeps the route, stripes the ski jump and hangs a stat point and the VV logo on its first leg
remakeChanges: Tape unchanged: sculpture → building ledge → next building → roof → 'the big ramp' (PS12); ski jump edged in red and green (LP12 34:29)
S described as 'at the top of the stairs to the tall building' (probably the same bridge top)
K inside the final balcony room; T via a planter quarter pipe → ledge → building; E via a ramp to a large window, above a small pool (same rooms)
New goals: 5 life preservers, Nosegrab the Hubba Gap, 5-0 Around the Fountain
New gaps: Around The Fountain, Hubba Hop, Ledge Hop, Up The Spiral; Lombard Gap not listed
transfer: Climb-then-drop crystal ≈ 0.5-1 m above a glass dome ≈ 5-6 m up at the plaza centre; rooftop launch ramp ≈ 10-12 m higher and ≈ 15-20 m back aimed at it

Walkway chain: second-storey ledges ≈ 1.5-2 m wide, ollie gaps ≤ 6-8 m between buildings (within the ≈ 9.4 m cruise ollie), one narrow ramp; an edge rail so a grind (2.1 m snap) can rescue a drifting line
Sculpture trench as the readable entrance, launching onto the first walkway (named gap)
Speed phases: corner quarter pipe, trench, braking walkways, downhill roof ramp; a speed pad on the roof instead of a stats gate
Arrow geometry: point the final ramp at the crystal and stripe its edges
Interlocking secret rooms: a letter room's exit door onto a high platform from which experts reach the dome directly
Dedicated-run design or a checkpoint at the fountain so the climb stays repeatable
openQuestions: Heights of the walkways (≈ 4-7 m), the ski-jump roof (≈ 12-18 m) and the Pagoda (≈ 5-8 m), all inferred
Whether the tape is taken by the glass break or by an icon just above it
How the TAS gets from the T room's exit to the Pagoda roof
Whether stats really gate the tape (G1 says so; LP1's stats unknown)
